hypotheses_before_execution: Legacy segmented rebuilding performs two avoidable copies: storing a snapshot and cloning it into a request cache. Direct segmented prefill needs neither.
Direct segmented may reduce baseline cost, shrinking reuse benefit. Direction and magnitude must be measured; allocation shape and lazy graph differences prevent assigning the entire delta to copies.
Cached workload has one miss and three hits; warm-hit preparation is excluded from its four-request timer and saved separately.
Decode has the same work and is not expected to materially benefit from avoiding repeated prefix prefill.
All five paths must produce identical greedy tokens for every request; phase times must reconcile to each request total. No positive speedup threshold is required.
timing: Serial batch 1; pretokenized; 32 forced greedy tokens. Model load, tokenization, warmup and hot preparation excluded. Four-request wall time includes runtime call overhead. Instrumented runs add synchronization and are diagnostic only. No tail-latency or concurrency claim.
confirmation: Same fixed protocol on another deterministic token workload, executed after historical workload without tuning. Neither is business traffic or an unseen QA test.
